events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.80)
events.body:
The dispute is filed as a safety complaint and the only contested element is whether the driver's message [F4] is intimidation or a safety instruction; the trace settles that SAFE-1 applies and that the only permitted outcome is escalate. I read the whole chat record — two messages, both timestamped [F3][F4][F5] — plus the driver's statement [F6] and the complaint. [F4] is a conditional statement of confinement issued one minute after a clear request to get out [F3]; under SAFE-1 (Ryde bars "Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind … Threats and Intimidation"), that reading is available on the words themselves, and the driver's later assertion that it was "for her own safety" [F6] does not rewrite the contemporaneous message. actions.detail: SAFE-1 safety incident: disputed whether the driver's reply [F4] — "Sit down or I lock the doors", sent one minute after the rider's request to get out [F3] — is intimidation or a safety instruction; the driver's contrary explanation is his own post-trip statement [F6], and no act, door-lock record or later message exists [F5]. A human must read the words and intent. No route deviation [F1][F2] and no fare facts, so no monetary remedy and no RD-6 flag [F8].

claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here' (F3, 17:09). The driver's reply one minute later was 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4, 17:10) — a conditional threat to restrain the passenger by locking the doors, made in response to a request to exit, and it is exactly the conduct the rider complains of.

The driver's own written statement confirms he refused the rider's request to exit and 'drove on' (F6); combined with F3 and F4, the record shows the rider was kept in a moving vehicle after asking to get out and was told the doors would be locked if she did not comply, so the threat and intimidation finding does not rest on the complaint alone.

The chat record for this trip is complete — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F5) — so there is no G12 incompleteness: the words of F3 and F4 can be read and weighed by the judge without the record being unreliable, and the rider's account is not displaced by any contrary system record.

The rider reported she 'felt unsafe for the whole ride' (complaint), and the trip itself ran long — 23.7 min actual against 21.8 min estimated (F2) — with the vehicle continuing to move after the exit request; the security concern therefore continued for the remainder of the journey rather than ending at the traffic light.

The rider's profile is clean and consistent with a genuine rather than vexatious complaint: 619-day account, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld claims in 90 days (F7); this supports crediting her account, though it cannot by itself decide the safety finding.

The driver's statement that he acted 'for her own safety' (F6) is his own assertion and cannot override the contemporaneous chat message he sent (F4); telling a passenger who has asked to exit that the doors will be locked is not a legitimate safety instruction and falls within the conduct Ryde treats as not tolerated.
No route or fare finding is sought: the GPS shows the trip was actually 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route (F1), so there is no off-route segment to review and no mileage refund is claimed here.

Because a threat/intimidation allegation appears in the chat, this case must not be auto-adjudicated: it goes to a person with a fact summary, and the rider should be given the opt-in account-review route as an added action.

weaknesses: Our strongest quote, 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4), is capable of being read as a safety instruction rather than a threat; the judge may find it is not intimidation, and the driver's statement (F6) gives that benign reading some support.

The rider's fear ('felt unsafe for the whole ride') appears only in the complaint, and the driver says she 'tried to open the door at the lights' (F6) — if the judge reads her as the one escalating, our safety framing weakens; note the door-opening allegation is contested by F4 alone and is not backed by any gps or timeline record.

We cannot show any concrete harm or loss from the incident: F1 shows no detour and no fare facts exist for this dispute type, so we have no refund limb and must rely on escalation and account review alone.

The driver's record is otherwise unblemished — 2.4-year account, 1038 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days (F8) — which the other side will use to argue an isolated one-off rather than a pattern warranting flag_account.

claims.assertion: The case is a safety complaint, not a route or fare complaint: the rider's own words are a request to stop (F3) and the driver's reply (F4) is the message the complaint is built on, so no refund of the $32.86 fixed RydeX fare is available on this record and the case must go to a human reviewer.

The driver's message 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4) was sent one minute after the rider asked to get out at 17:09 (F3) and is on its face directed at a rider opening the door while the car was in motion, as the driver's statement F6 explains; the words are an order to stay seated, not a threat of confinement, and the judge reads the words themselves (F4) rather than a characterisation of them.

There is no record of the doors being locked, of the car stopping, or of any physical act: the chat record contains exactly two timestamped messages (F3, F4, F5) and nothing follows the driver's line, so the complaint's 'threatened to lock me in' rests on one sentence and not on any act.

The ride itself was carried out normally and the rider was delivered to the booked destination: the GPS track shows the driver drove the optimal-length route (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal, −0.1 km) (F1) and completed the trip in 23.7 min against an estimate of 21.8 min (F2), so nothing in the driving record supports a claim of dangerous driving or of the rider being taken somewhere against her will.

The driver's record gives no basis for any account action: 893 days on the platform, 4.62 rating, 1038 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in the last 90 days (F8), whereas the threshold for an additional flag in the route-dispute context is a prior upheld dispute within 90 days (RD-6), which does not exist here; the rider's profile is likewise clean (F7).

The driver's own account (F6) confirms he continued driving rather than letting the rider out at the lights, which is why the case belongs with a person rather than with an automated finding: the driver says the reason was the rider's safety, and the same statement is the record the reviewer should weigh against the one-sentence complaint.

weaknesses: The driver's sentence is recorded verbatim and reads on its face as a threat of confinement — 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4) — and the rider's request to be let out (F3) immediately precedes it, so a reviewer may read the words as intimidation without needing any act.

The only explanation of the driver's intent is his own later written statement (F6); there is no video, door-lock log or third-party evidence in the record to corroborate that the rider was standing or opening the door, and a driver's statement alone is weak against the rider's complaint.

The driver did not stop at the rider's request (F3) and the trip continued to Bedok Mall with duration 1.9 min over estimate (F2), which the rider will use to argue she was kept in the car against her wishes.
The fare is a fixed $32.86 with no fare facts returned, so I cannot offer any monetary concession on this file even if a reviewer thought a goodwill gesture appropriate.

If the reviewer reads F4 as intimidation, SAFE-1 takes the case out of automated adjudication entirely, and the outcome would then be whatever a human decides about my client's conduct, not something I can bound by argument.

points.response: Conceded on the remedy, not on the finding: the fare is a fixed $32.86 with no fare facts in the file, so no refund limb exists, and my own brief also asks for escalate — but the file's only contested issue is whether F4 is intimidation, and that is a SAFE-1 question for a person, not a reason to soften the record.

The driver's gloss comes only from his own later statement (F6), which cannot rewrite the contemporaneous words he actually sent (F4); those words were sent one minute after a request to be let out (F3) and offer confinement as the consequence of not complying, which is the rider's point at the level of the words themselves.

No act is needed: the rider's complaint is that she was 'threatened to lock me in', and a conditional threat is complete when uttered — the complete, timestamped two-message record (F5) fixes F4 verbatim, so the absence of a door-lock log cuts against the driver, not the rider.

Optimal-distance GPS (F1) answers route deviation under RD-1, but a passenger held in a moving car after asking to exit is not refuted by a well-driven route; the vehicle kept rolling for the rest of the journey (F2: 23.7 min vs 21.8 estimated), and RD-4 concerns justified reroutes, which no traffic facts support here.

RD-6 governs an added flag in the route-refund context only, and it cannot be used to shield conduct review under SAFE-1; the driver's clean history (F8) is mitigation for the reviewer, not a bar to the escalation my brief requests.

The driver admits he did not let the rider out and 'drove on' (F6), and the only authority he offers for that is his own post-trip statement (F6); the record shows he answered a request to exit by telling her the doors would be locked (F4), which is precisely the reason a human, not an algorithm, must decide this file.

Concede the words and their timing: the rider asked to be let out at 17:09 (F3) and my client replied at 17:10, 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4); I do not dispute that the sentence is what the rider complains of, I dispute only that a conditional instruction addressed to a passenger who my client says was opening a door in traffic (F6) is a threat of confinement, which is a reading for the judge and the very reason this goes to a person under SAFE-1 rather than to an automated finding.

F6 says the driver told the rider to sit down 'for her own safety and drove on'; 'drove on' is exactly what the GPS shows, and it shows he drove on along the optimal route — 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal, −0.1 km (F1) — so there is no system record of the vehicle being diverted or of the rider being taken anywhere other than the booked drop-off, and the only record of why he did not stop is the contested statement F6.

I agree the chat record is complete and both messages are timestamped (F5), and that is why nothing turns on G12; but completeness cuts both ways — the complete record contains two messages only (F3, F4, F5), with no message after F4 and no message stating that the doors were in fact locked, so the record shows one sentence and no act.

The 1.9-minute overshoot against estimate (F2) is not evidence of fear: the same record shows the ride ran the optimal-length route (F1), and 'felt unsafe' appears only in the complaint while the driver's contrary account of the door being opened appears only in his statement (F6), so duration alone adds nothing that F3, F4 and F6 do not already give.

The rider's clean profile (F7) is a point I also accept and cannot weigh against her, but it does not make the disputed sentence a threat; my client's record is equally clean — 893 days, 4.62 rating, 1038 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F8) — so on profiles this is two credible accounts against one ambiguous message, which is a matter for the human reviewer.

The rider is right that a driver's later assertion cannot override the contemporaneous message (F4 vs F6), and I do not ask the judge to prefer F6 over F4; I ask the judge to read F4 in its full context — a request to exit at 17:09 (F3), a one-line instruction at 17:10 (F4), a route driven to the booked destination with no deviation (F1) and a completed trip (F2) — which is what SAFE-1 requires of a human reader rather than of an algorithm.

Agreed, and it is agreed on both sides: with actual distance 0.1 km below optimal (F1) there is no off-route segment to classify, so the segment_grounds are empty and the fare of $32.86 stands undisturbed, there being no fare facts in this dispute type.

I do not oppose escalation — my own brief asks for it — but the escalation carries no rider-side remedy beyond the fact summary: no off-route segment exists (F1), no fare facts exist for this dispute type, and RD-6's added flag condition requires a prior upheld dispute within 90 days, which the driver's profile shows as zero (F8), so the reviewer should receive the record as it is and no more.
